title: Yoga Sutras of Patanjali
description: The foundational text of Yoga philosophy, consisting of 196 sutras organized into four chapters (padas).

The transformation of control is the emergence of control impressions and the subsidence of emergence impressions.
Its peaceful flow comes from impression.
The transformation of samadhi is the decline of scattered attention and the rise of one-pointedness.
The transformation of one-pointedness is when subsiding and arising impressions are equal.
By this, the transformations of property, character, and condition in elements and senses are explained.
The substratum is that which runs through the past, present, and future properties.
Difference in sequence is the cause of different transformations.
By samyama on the three transformations comes knowledge of past and future.
Word, meaning, and idea are normally confused; by samyama on their distinction comes knowledge of all sounds.
By bringing latent impressions to consciousness comes knowledge of previous births.
From samyama on another's mind comes knowledge of their thoughts.
But not of the underlying basis, as that is not the object of samyama.
By samyama on the form of the body, when its visibility is suspended, there is invisibility.

blocks.content: सोपक्रमं निरुपक्रमं च कर्म तत्संयमादपरान्तज्ञानमरिष्टेभ्यो वा
blocks.transliteration: sopakramaṃ nirupakramaṃ ca karma tatsaṃyamādaparāntajñānamariṣṭebhyo vā
blocks.meaning: Similarly, disappearance of sound and other senses.
Karma is fast or slow; by samyama on it, or on omens, comes knowledge of death.
By samyama on friendliness, etc., those powers arise.
By samyama on strength, the strength of an elephant, etc.
By directing the light of superphysical perception, knowledge of the subtle, hidden, and distant arises.
By samyama on the sun, knowledge of the worlds.
On the moon, knowledge of the arrangement of stars.
On the pole star, knowledge of their movements.
On the navel center, knowledge of the body's arrangement.
On the throat pit, cessation of hunger and thirst.
On the kurma nadi, steadiness.
On the light at the crown of the head, vision of the perfected ones.
Or from intuitive illumination, all knowledge.
On the heart, understanding of the mind.
Experience arises from non-distinction between purusha and sattva, which are absolutely different. By samyama on self-interest vs. interest in the Self, comes knowledge of purusha.
From that arise intuitive hearing, touching, seeing, tasting, and smelling.
These are obstacles to samadhi but accomplishments in the worldly state.
By loosening the cause of bondage and knowing the passages, the mind enters another's body.
By mastery over udana, there is non-contact with water, mud, thorns, etc., and rising above.
By mastery over samana, blazing radiance.
By samyama on the relation between ear and space, divine hearing.
By samyama on the relation between body and space, and by absorption in lightness, passage through space.
The external, unfancied modification is the great disembodied; from that, the covering of light disappears.
By samyama on the gross, essential nature, subtle, interconnection, and purpose of elements, mastery over them.
From that comes minuteness, etc., perfection of body, and non-obstruction of its functions.
Perfection of body is beauty, grace, strength, and adamantine hardness.
By samyama on grasping, essential nature, I-am-ness, interconnection, and purpose, mastery over the senses.
From that, swiftness of mind, perception without instruments, and mastery over prakriti.
Only from discernment of the difference between sattva and purusha comes sovereignty over all states and omniscience.
By non-attachment even to that, the seed of bondage is destroyed, and kaivalya results.
There should be no pride or attachment upon invitation by celestials, for undesirable consequences may recur.
By samyama on moment and its succession comes wisdom born of discrimination.
From that comes discernment of two similar things not distinguishable by class, character, or position.
Discriminative wisdom is liberating, encompasses all objects and all times, and is non-sequential.
When sattva and purusha are equally pure, there is kaivalya.
The subtler attainments
The transition or
The incidental cause does not move the natural tendencies; it merely removes obstacles, like a farmer.
Created minds arise from ego alone.
One mind directs the many in their various activities.
Of these, the one born of meditation is free from impressions.
The karma of a yogi is neither white nor black; of others, it is threefold.
From that, only those tendencies manifest for which conditions are favorable.
Memory and impressions are of the same form, so there is continuity even when separated by birth, place, and time.
They are without beginning, due to the perpetuity of desire.
Being held together by cause, result, support, and object, they cease when those cease.
Past and future exist in reality, in different forms according to the paths of properties.
They are manifest or subtle according to the nature of the gunas.
The uniqueness of transformation is due to the unity of change.
Due to the difference in minds, the same object is perceived differently.

blocks.content: न चैकचित्ततन्त्रं वस्तु तदप्रमाणकं तदा किं स्यात्
blocks.transliteration: na caikacittatantraṃ vastu tadapramāṇakaṃ tadā kiṃ syāt
blocks.meaning: An object is not dependent on one mind; what would happen to it when not cognized by that mind?
An object is known or unknown depending on whether the mind is colored by it.
The modifications of the mind are always known by its lord, the changeless purusha.
The mind is not self-luminous, being an object of perception.
And there cannot be cognition of both at the same time.
If cognition by another mind were postulated, there would be infinite regress and confusion of memories.
When consciousness assumes the form of that which does not move, self-knowledge becomes possible.
The mind, colored by both seer and seen, comprehends everything.
Though variegated by countless impressions, the mind exists for another, because it acts in association.
For one who sees the distinction, reflection on the nature of the self ceases.
Then the mind inclines toward discrimination and gravitates toward liberation.
In the intervals of that, other thoughts arise from impressions.
Their removal is like that of the afflictions, as described.
For one who has no interest even in the highest knowledge, constant discriminative discernment brings the samadhi called dharma-megha.
From that, afflictions and karma cease.
Then, with all coverings and impurities removed, what remains to be known is little, due to the infinity of knowledge.
From that, the gunas have fulfilled their purpose, and their sequence of transformation comes to an end.
Sequence corresponds to moments, apprehensible at the end of transformation.

blocks.content: पुरुषार्थशून्यानां गुणानां प्रतिप्रसवः कैवल्यं स्वरूपप्रतिष्ठा वा चितिशक्तिरिति
blocks.transliteration: puruṣārthaśūnyānāṃ guṇānāṃ pratiprasavaḥ kaivalyaṃ svarūpapratiṣṭhā vā citiśaktiriti
blocks.meaning: Kaivalya is the involution of the gunas, no longer serving the purpose of purusha, or the establishment of the power of consciousness in its own nature.
